newsitem.title: USA: US Plains wheat evades further freeze damage - WSC.
newsitem.headline: US Plains wheat evades further freeze damage - WSC.

text.p: Overnight temperatures in the U.S. Central Plains Tuesday were not cold enough to cause further damage to the the hard red winter wheat crop, a U.S. meteorolgist said Wednesday.
"We saw nothing serious in terms of temperatures," said Joel Burgio, senior meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass.

The coldest temperatures were seen in southern Nebraska, where overnight lows were in the upper 20s (degrees Fahrenheit). Lows in Kansas ranged from 32 degrees in the north, to 35 degrees in the southeast, Burgio said.
In Oklahoma, the low in the northwest portion of the state was 44 degrees, and the southeastern low was 52 degrees, Burgio said.
"Again, the important thing is the weekend weather and how much damage was done due to that freeze," Burgio said.

Damage to the hard red winter wheat crop is still being assessed, but early estimates show moderate to severe damage in Kansas, which is the nation's top wheat growing state, agronomists said Tuesday.
The developing crops in Texas and Oklahoma were also seen sustaining serious damage.
Much warmer temperatures are expected in the next several days, Burgio said.
"After tomorrow morning, it warms up considerably," Burgio said.
Low temperatures on Thursday morning will be in the 30s and 40s in the Southern Plains, but will warm up into the 60s and 70s during the day, Burgio said.
"On Friday, the temperatures are forecast to warm up into the 70s and possibly the 80s, so we're looking at a pretty strong warm-up in the next couple of days," Burgio said.
